title: Implementation and Validation of Titratable Cysteine in GROMACS-based Constant-pH Molecular Dynamics
tldr:
### Problem
The study aims to address the challenge of maintaining constant pH during molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, particularly for systems containing titratable cysteine residues.

### Method
The authors propose a method that integrates the protonation state of cysteine into the GROMACS-based Constant-pH MD simulation by using a modified Berendsen coupling algorithm.

### Dataset / Benchmark
The work evaluates the proposed method on a model system consisting of a protein with multiple cysteine residues in an aqueous solution.

### Key Findings
- The implementation of titratable cysteine significantly improves the pH stability during simulations, reducing fluctuations by up to 50%.
- The modified Berendsen coupling algorithm maintains a more accurate pH value compared to the standard GROMACS method.
- The proposed approach shows promising results in preserving the native structure of proteins with cysteine residues during constant-pH MD simulations.

### Why It Matters
This work provides a valuable tool for drug discovery, computational chemistry, and molecular machine learning by enabling more accurate and stable simulations of protein systems containing titratable cysteine residues, which are common in many biological macromolecules.
